nodes.answer: Reviewing LCAs is crucial because it helps understand the various life-cycle environmental impacts and uncertainties associated with different CDR technologies.

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of the research outlined in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of the research is to develop a critical understanding of the employment of digital technologies for LCA studies, focusing on the opportunities and challenges associated with circular strategies.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Purpose This research aims to develop a critical understanding of the employment of digital technologies (DTs) for LCA studies, outlining both the opportunities and challenges associated with circular strategies. Two research questions are thus addressed: (1) What circular loops and aspects are addressed when digital technologies are integrated in the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? (2) Which trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle? Methods This study is based on the problematisation approach, which critically examines existing assumptions in the LCA literature, structured into six principles: defining a domain of investigation, articulating and evaluating assumptions, develop- ing alternative perspectives, involving the audience through qualitative interviews, and assessing the alternative assumptions. A systematic literature review (SLR) and semi-structured interviews with experts were conducted to explore these issues and suggest future research directions. Results and discussion It emerges that the DTs are mainly integrated in the Life Cycle Inventory phase capturing closing and narrowing loops, whereas a limited number of cases investigate slowing loops with different aspects investigated.

nodes.question: What is the purpose of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: LCA quantifies the environmental impacts of products or services throughout their entire lifecycle to support environmental sustainability assessments and circular economy strategies.

In this perspective, the circular paradigm contributes to decoupling economic growth from the intensive use of natural resources (Chen et al. 2020 ; Lei et al. 2021 ), thus contributing to the sustainable development goals (SDGs). Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is among the most widely adopted methodologies for quantifying the environmen- tal impacts of products or services throughout their entire lifecycle, providing a robust basis for environmental sus- tainability assessments and circular economy strategies (Hellweg and Mil i Canals 2014; ISO 2020a; Lei et al. 2021; Br ndstr m and Saidani 2022; Sica et al. 2022). LCA consists of four main steps, namely, goal and scope definition, Life Cycle Inventory (LCI), Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA), and interpretation of results (ISO 2020a; ISO 2020b). nodes.question: Why is the integration of digital technologies into LCA considered complex?
nodes.answer: It is considered complex because it is still at an early stage of study and implementation.

This approach boosts innovation in production processes and improves corporate sustainability, fostering the twin digi - tal and circular transition (Nascimento et al. 2019; Bai et al. 2020 ; Bocken et al. 2023). Despite the benefits, integrating digital technologies into LCA is a complex process as it is still at an early stage of study and implementation (Wang et al. 2019; Sica et al. 2022). The main barriers to improvements in these terms include the need for advanced technical skills to implement and manage these technologies, high initial costs associated with the adoption of new digital infrastructure, and resistance to change within organisations (Farooque et al. 2020; Ruggieri et al. 2020). In addition, the lack of standardi- sation and interoperability between different digital tools and platforms can complicate data integration and hinder the effec- tiveness of assessments (Ghita et al. 2021 ). nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main aim of the research mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main aim of the research is to develop a deeper and more critical understanding of the integration of digital technologies (DTs) into Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), focusing on the opportunities and challenges of circular strategies.
nodes.paragraph: 2020; Sica et al. 2022) Moving from this background, this research aims to develop a deeper and more critical understanding of the integration of DTs into LCA, outlining both the opportuni- ties and challenges associated with circular strategies. To this end, this research questions existing assumptions and develops new research perspectives. Emerging positions from the literature regarding the role of DTs for LCA studies are discussed, with a specific focus on the Life Cycle Inven- tory (LCI). Specifically, the research questions that guided the study are the following: RQ1: What circular loops are addressed when digital technologies are integrated into the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? RQ2: What trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle? The findings of this study are expected to contribute to the existing body of knowledge on LCA by providing detailed insights into how DTs can enhance the development of LCI, promoting the business circular transition. Additionally, the study offers practical recommendations for organisations seeking to implement these technologies to achieve more sustainable and efficient production systems.

nodes.question: What does Life Cycle Management (LCM) entail?
nodes.answer: Life Cycle Management (LCM) is a dynamic and iterative process that involves engaging various stakeholders. It is informed by Life Cycle Analysis (LCA) data but goes beyond environmental factors to consider economic and social dimensions for a comprehensive approach to sustainable development.
